HOW IT WORKS

blocks.text: The technique and the science work as one
blocks.html: The technique and the science work as one
Two massage techniques form the core of the treatment. Active ingredients from the Anesi Cellular 3 range are applied at each stage, chosen to reinforce and extend what the hands are doing.
Lymphatic drainage
Light, rhythmic strokes that guide stagnant fluid away from the face toward the lymph nodes in the neck and collarbone. Reduces puffiness, clears congestion, and restores natural clarity and tone.
Connective tissue massage
Deeper, deliberate work on the fascia beneath the skin. Releases adhesions, stimulates collagen production, and remodels facial contours for firmer definition.
Cellular 3 Peel
Nano-encapsulated hydroxy acids combined with enzymatic exfoliation clear the skin’s surface and prepare it to absorb the active ingredients that follow.
Cellular 3 Concentrate

Applied during connective tissue massage at the highest concentration of Progeline, Malt Secret, and 3GF Complex — protecting structural proteins, neutralising oxidative stress, and stimulating cellular renewal.
Cellular 3 Hyaluronic Mask
A low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid mask applied after massage to increase hydration, improve elasticity, and plump fine lines from within.

Each session runs 75 minutes. The connective tissue massage is performed one side of the face at a time — first with the concentrate applied, then with renewal cream during the drainage phase — so that every minute of hands-on work is supported by active ingredients at their point of use.

blocks.text: HOW IT WORKS WHY IT MATTERS
blocks.html: HOW IT WORKS WHY IT MATTERS
Three Pathways. One Restorative Treatment.

From our mid-thirties, the face begins to age along three distinct pathways that surface-level care cannot fully address. First, a slower lymphatic flow can lead to puffiness and a duller tone. Beneath that, the fascia — the skin’s inner support — loses its natural bounce and stiffens, blurring your facial contours. Finally, a process called glycation makes collagen and elastin more rigid, leading to fine lines and wrinkles.

The Lymphatic Sculpt Facial addresses all three levels at once:
– Gentle lymphatic drainage clears the fluid buildup that can make the face look puffy or flat.
– Expert connective tissue massage releases tension in the fascia, restoring the natural lift and definition of your contours.

– Cellular 3 active ingredients — including Progeline and 3GF Complex — work at the cellular level to protect your skin’s structural proteins, interrupt the glycation process, and spark its own renewal.

FAQS
Common questions

blocks.text: How is the Lymphatic Sculpt Facial different from a standard facial?
blocks.html: How is the Lymphatic Sculpt Facial different from a standard facial?

Most facials focus on the skin’s surface — cleansing, exfoliating, and applying products. The Lymphatic Sculpt Facial works on the structures beneath the skin: the lymphatic system and the fascia. This means the results — reduced puffiness, clearer tone, firmer contour — are driven by what the therapist’s hands do, supported by active ingredients that work at the cellular level. The Anesi Cellular 3 products are not applied as finishing steps; they are used during the massage to reinforce the technique at each stage.

blocks.text: How many sessions does it take to see results?
blocks.html: How many sessions does it take to see results?

Some clients notice reduced puffiness and improved tone after a single session. Structural changes — improved contour, firmer skin, visible reduction in fine lines — develop over a course of treatment. Ten monthly sessions is the recommended programme for sustained results, which reflects the cumulative nature of both fascia remodelling and cellular renewal. A course is a considered investment; the results compound in ways a one-off session cannot deliver.

blocks.text: Is the treatment suitable for sensitive skin?
blocks.html: Is the treatment suitable for sensitive skin?

Yes. The lymphatic drainage component uses light, rhythmic pressure — it is one of the gentler techniques in facial therapy. The Cellular 3 active ingredients are formulated for all skin types, including dry and sensitive. The connective tissue massage involves more deliberate pressure on the fascia, but this should not cause discomfort; your therapist adjusts depth based on what the skin and tissue are telling them. If you have a specific skin condition, mention it when you book and your therapist will advise accordingly.
